title: Lucent Ventures — Partner deal orchestration & pipeline scrub
summary: Quarterly pipeline scrub with Lucent to prioritize co-sell opportunities, align on handoffs and identify action items for three prioritized deals. Talk covered technical fit, routing play, executive sponsorship and a short win/loss landscape overview.
next_steps: Maya to send Lucent co-sell playbook and joint pitch deck by 2026-01-20
Jordan to coordinate a 1-hour Netlytics POC benchmark with Lucent infra by 2026-01-23
Lucas to update joint opportunities in Salesforce and tag Redwood partnership by 2026-01-19
Schedule executive intro (Redwood VP+Lucent GM) by end of Jan
action_items: Maya — share co-sell playbook, deck, and pricing matrix (due 2026-01-20)
Jordan — spin up quick smoke benchmark for Netlytics POC and share perf notes (due 2026-01-23)
Lucas — prioritize Arcadia Health and Netlytics opportunities in Salesforce and add opportunity owners (due 2026-01-19)
Nina — confirm regional contact points for APAC pilot (due 2026-01-21)
transcript:
Header: 2026-01-17 09:42 PT | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Lucas (Lucent Head of Partnerships), Nina (Lucent Channel Lead), Omar (Lucent Sales Ops)
---
Summary: quick scrub of top partner-sourced deals and orchestration playbook for March close window.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see folks on; quick check on audio.
[00:12] Lucas Reed: Yeah can you hear me, Maya?
[00:15] Maya Patel: Loud and clear. Thanks for making time, Lucas, Nina, Omar. Agenda — prioritize the three ops you sent last week, go over the handoff, and call out any blockers.
[00:28] Nina Park: Sounds good. I'm on mobile so apologies if I drop — quick ask, can we focus on Arcadia Health and Netlytics first, those are the most time sensitive.
[00:37] Jordan Li: Great, will do. I pulled the technical notes from the spreadsheet you shared — thanks. A couple quick clarifying q's on Netlytics infra.
[00:45] Omar Singh: Yep go ahead.
[00:47] Jordan Li: For the Netlytics POC, do they want dedicated GPUs or is hosted okay? I saw some notes about regulatory constraints.
[00:55] Lucas Reed: Netlytics prefers dedicated for throughput, and they asked about an on-prem-ish pattern. Not full air gap but VPC and key management.
[01:05] Maya Patel: Okay so that maps to Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private. We should flag expected RPS and target latency so Jordan can size the cluster and give a cost estimate.
[01:17] Nina Park: On Arcadia, they care more about PII and audit logs; SSO and KMS questions came up in legal.
[01:24] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll attach SOC2 + audit doc in the playbook.
[01:28] Lucas Reed: Quick landscape — CloudMuse is in both accounts, and ModelServe came in for Arcadia last quarter. We need crisp differentiation on latency and deterministic pricing.
[01:40] Jordan Li: Understood. On the technical side, we can show a 99th percentile latency metric and a simple token-based cost per 1k that maps to their throughput profile.
[01:51] Omar Singh: Also, for sales ops, please use the tag "Lucent_Redwood" on the SFDC opp so it's easy to report. Right now some were tagged as "partner_co" and others as "referral" which confuses pipeline counts.
[02:05] Maya Patel: Good catch. Lucas, can you commit to a tagging cleanup?
[02:09] Lucas Reed: Yep, I can run a scrub and assign owners — but we may need one more data point: who is the executive sponsor on Redwood side? That will help elevate an opp.
[02:18] Maya Patel: I will loop in our VP of Partnerships, Claire Donovan. I'll ask Claire to do an intro for the top two deals.
[02:25] Nina Park: Perfect.
[02:28] [03:12] Jordan Li: Quick deep dive on Netlytics technical constraints — they use a streaming ingest and expect many short chat sessions with long KV context. We should check our KV cache behavior on the dedicated stack.
[03:30] Lucas Reed: Right, they called it "context stitching" in their app notes. It's not massive but they do retain 8–12k tokens per session in some cases.
[03:40] Jordan Li: Okay that's helpful. We'll note the sequence length distribution and pick a model variant that handles long context without heavy cost. Might suggest quantization + batching strategy to hit the SLOs.
[03:52] Maya Patel: Jordan, can you estimate cost delta between hosted + caching vs dedicated? The customer will want a delta for procurement.
[04:01] Jordan Li: Off the cuff, for sustained 100QPS with 2k avg context, dedicated is typically 25–40% cheaper at scale, but burst handling and autoscale policies affect that. I'll run numbers in a follow-up doc.
[04:15] Omar Singh: For procurement, we need clear SLAs and a baseline TCO for a year.
[04:21] Maya Patel: We'll include a 12-month TCO scenario in the playbook.
[04:24] [06:00] Lucas Reed: Switching to Arcadia — they are risk-averse, and legal asked about our retention and deletion guarantees. Also FIPS for keys was mentioned.
[06:10] Jordan Li: We support KMS integrations and can map to FIPS-certified modules in Private deployments. For audit logs, we can enable per-tenant retention policies.
[06:19] Nina Park: One more: Arcadia's team is in APAC; latency from NA regions was a concern.
[06:25] Jordan Li: We can route via APAC region, though that depends on capacity. There is a potential fallback to a smaller local model if budget doesn't allow full scale.
[06:36] Maya Patel: That's that graceful degradation bit — important to document in the canary/fallback section.
[06:42] [08:15] Omar Singh: On co-sell motion — Lucent sales reps want clear rules: who owns the first meeting, who responds to RFPs, and when to involve execs. Can we put a 3-step handoff?
[08:27] Maya Patel: Yes. Proposal: 1) Lucent qualifies and books intro; 2) Redwood AE/SE join demo and propose pilot scope; 3) Joint exec alignment for commercial terms. We'll put roles on the playbook.
[08:40] Lucas Reed: Works. Also, can we have a shared calendar for pilot milestones? Helps us manage expectations.
[08:47] Jordan Li: We'll create a Google calendar and a short milestone doc.
[08:51] [10:00] Maya Patel: Quick question on incentives — Lucent, do you expect a referral fee or a co-sell split?
[10:06] Lucas Reed: Usually a revenue share on closed-won, but for strategic accounts we prefer a fixed rev share plus joint marketing credits. We can confirm exact numbers via contract.
[10:17] Maya Patel: We'll draft a commercial appendix and share it.
[10:20] Nina Park: Also, in-regions marketing — Lucent can run webinars with our product team for APAC/EMEA in Feb if we can commit to a case study.
[10:31] Maya Patel: We'll prioritize Arcadia as a potential case study if the pilot runs.
[10:35] [12:10] Jordan Li: Back to Netlytics — performance benchmark ask: they want 95th and 99th percentiles for a 2k token window under 50 RPS sustained for 15 minutes. We can run this in our staging cluster.
[12:22] Omar Singh: Timing?
[12:24] Jordan Li: I can run it next week with a small slot; need credentials and sample prompt shapes.
[12:30] Lucas Reed: I'll send sample prompt shapes today.
[12:33] Jordan Li: Great. Also note — the transcripts from previous POCs have minor mislabels like K V cash instead of K V cache, so please excuse if our earlier notes had weird terms.
[12:45] [14:00] Maya Patel: On tracking, Omar, what's the current number of open Lucent-sourced opps in pipeline?
[14:07] Omar Singh: Right now Lucent has 18 open opps in SFDC, 6 in late-stage, 3 we marked as high priority for Q1.
[14:15] Maya Patel: Let's focus on those three: Arcadia Health, Netlytics, and TidalWorks. Are there any legal/regulatory blockers for TidalWorks?
[14:24] Lucas Reed: TidalWorks wants data residency in EU. They may prefer a private deployment in EMEA.
[14:32] Jordan Li: We have Private deployments that can run in the customer's VPC in EMEA — need to check network connectivity and HSM/KMS options.
[14:40] Nina Park: Fine — I'll get the EMEA infra contacts and share.
[14:45] [16:05] Maya Patel: Competitive positioning — Lucas you mentioned CloudMuse. Where did they win and why?
[16:12] Lucas Reed: CloudMuse nailed a price and an easier procurement contract with a smaller SOC addendum; their latency was okay for the use case. We should emphasize our deterministic pricing and the auditing capability.
[16:27] Jordan Li: We also have stronger observability: token-level breakdowns and per-route tracing which helps ops teams. We'll prepare a quick slide.
[16:37] Maya Patel: Great.
[16:40] [18:30] Omar Singh: Ops ask — is there a simple checklist for deployment readiness we can attach to opps? Things like SSO, KMS, network, capacity, data residency.
[18:40] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll add a 1-page checklist to the playbook. Jordan will own the technical checklist.
[18:45] Jordan Li: I'll draft and share it.
[18:50] [21:00] Lucas Reed: Question on booking motions — If a deal wants a 6-week POC, how do we price and run it without the customer feeling constrained?
[21:10] Maya Patel: We usually do a time-boxed pilot with capped usage and a pilot fee. For larger partners we can do a credit-based pilot and roll into committed capacity if they convert. We'll put pricing buckets in the appendix.
[21:23] Nina Park: Good. Can we get sample SOW language for pilot scope?
[21:28] Maya Patel: Yes, legal has a template. I'll attach it.
[21:33] [24:00] Jordan Li: Technical note: for the Netlytics POC, if they insist on on-prem with HSM, that will add 2–3 weeks to provisioning. We need to call that out to avoid slipped timelines.
[24:12] Lucas Reed: Copy that. We'll surface that to the customer.
[24:16] Omar Singh: For tracking, we need one canonical doc — some of the opportunities had duplicate rows across our spreadsheets. Can we consolidate into the shared playbook?
[24:26] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll make the playbook the single source of truth and include a short ops section for SFDC ownership.
[24:33] [27:00] Lucas Reed: I'd like to propose a joint weekly 30-minute sync for Q1 to keep momentum.
[27:08] Maya Patel: Fine by us. Jordan and I can do Tuesdays 9am PT. Does that work?
[27:14] Nina Park: Works on our side. We'll set a recurring invite.
[27:19] [30:00] Jordan Li: Quick item — any constraints on sharing internal benchmarks? Some customers want anonymized logs for evaluation. We can share synthetic traces and anonymized perf runs.
[30:10] Lucas Reed: Anonymized is fine. Arcadia asked for sample audit logs to validate retention.
[30:18] Jordan Li: We'll generate a sanitized log sample.
[30:22] [33:00] Maya Patel: Let's do a quick recap of the top three action items so folks leave with clear owners. Jordan?
[33:08] Jordan Li: I'll run the Netlytics benchmark (95/99 pctl) next week and share the report.
[33:14] Maya Patel: I'll send the co-sell playbook, deck, pricing appendix, and SOW template by Tue. Lucas?
[33:21] Lucas Reed: I'll clean up the SFDC tags and assign owners, and I'll circulate the sample prompts.
[33:28] Nina Park: I'll confirm APAC/EMEA infra contacts and the regional marketing window.
[33:34] Omar Singh: I'll set up the shared calendar and create the SFDC report for partner-sourced opps.
[33:40] [35:50] Maya Patel: Anything else?
[35:52] Lucas Reed: One tiny flag — TidalWorks has a procurement freeze until Feb 1, so push on timing.
[35:59] Maya Patel: Noted; we'll focus on Arcadia and Netlytics for early Q1 plays.
[36:05] [40:00] Jordan Li: For the benchmark run I'll need a list of prompt shapes and a test account. Lucas, can you share creds?
[40:09] Lucas Reed: I'll share credentials via the secure doc after the call.
[40:14] Jordan Li: Great. Also, for the on-prem scenario, will Lucent provision the HSM or do we route to our provider?
[40:22] Nina Park: We prefer to use customer's HSM, but if that becomes a blocker we can discuss alternatives.
[40:29] Jordan Li: Okay we'll note both options in the checklist.
[40:35] [44:00] Maya Patel: I'll follow up with Claire to get exec intro. Plan is to do the intro once we have Netlytics perf report.
[44:08] Lucas Reed: Sounds good.
[44:12] [47:30] Omar Singh: Scheduling note — can the weekly sync start 2026-01-27?
[47:36] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll start the weekly on the 27th. Invite after this call.
[47:41] Nina Park: I'll send the invite.
[47:44] [50:00] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — we'll share the materials and action items. Appreciate Lucent's partnership.
[50:08] Lucas Reed: Thanks Maya and team. Looking forward to the benchmark.
[50:12] Jordan Li: Thanks all.
[50:15] [52:00] End of call.
